text:
alex: quick heads-up — ran a long tail perf run on the new kernel-selection heuristic and saw a 12% increase in OOMs on 16GB cards under mixed short+long workloads. attaching notes below.
monica: ugh. do you have a minimal repro?
sahil: can you paste the allocator stats dump? wondering if fragmentation spiked or it's just peak working set.
alex: dump attached inline: 
```
kv_alloc_stats: total_free=1.2GiB total_used=14.8GiB slabs=128 frag_metric=0.37 largest_free_chunk=48MiB
workspace_usage: avg=9.2MiB p50=6MiB p95=120MiB p99=420MiB
prefill_hits=68% decode_hits=32% active_prefill=2100 items
```
alex: fragmentation is the suspect — frag_metric jumped from ~0.12 to 0.37 after kernel change that prefers fused matmul kernels for long sequences. we moved some intermediate buffers to persistent workspace which made many medium-sized allocations stick around.
kai: that matches what I saw in microbench — fused kernels allocate many 64–256KiB buffers, and our slab binning ends up with lots of half-used slabs.
monica: do we know whether OOMs happen during prefill or decode phases? different mitigation paths.
alex: most OOMs in traces are during decode (beam expansion spikes), but prefill-length requests increase baseline fragmentation so decode can't fit. sequence: large prefill -> persist small buffers -> decode spike -> fail.
sahil: two levers: 1) tighten per-request caps for prefill (cap persistent workspace per-request) 2) compact/evict small slabs proactively when fragmentation > threshold. both have tradeoffs.
monica: can we try soft caps first (throttle prefill growth) — less risky. set per-request workspace cap to 256MiB for 16GB nodes and failover to decode-only kernel if > cap.
kai: I sketched a quick patch: add `kv_prefill_soft_cap` config and a fallback route. pseudo: 
```
if (prefill_working_set > kv_prefill_soft_cap) {
  route_request(kernel=decode_friendly, prefilling=false)
}
```
kai: also added an allocator probe to record bin occupancy histogram every 10s. it'll help verify frag spikes.
infra-bot: alert: node pool gpu-16gb-1 observed 4 OOM events in 1h (avg mem used 96%). See /ops/oom-alerts/2745 for traces.
monica: nice. timeline for experiment? can we A/B toggle on 10% of traffic to dedicated canary region?
sahil: I'll run a stress job that simulates mixed-short-long traffic with our new probe and collect histograms. plan: baseline (master), kernel-change-only, kernel+soft-cap, kernel+aggressive-evict. each run 4h.
alex: perf numbers from a quick local run (toy model) — baseline error rate 0.2%, kernel-change 0.9%, +soft-cap 0.3% but latency 6% higher p95 for long-seq.
kai: the latency hit makes sense — falling back to decode-friendly kernels increases per-token cost. but reliability improves.
monica: acceptable if reliability is restored. try to optimize the decode-friendly path (kernel tuning) to reduce p95. also open a regression test that fails CI when frag_metric > 0.25 under synthetic load.
sahil: adding perf test: `make perf-run PROFILE=kv-frag TEST=short-long-mix DURATION=30m` — will push as part of nightly.
alex: in parallel, I propose we implement a lightweight slab-coalescer during low-util windows: scan adjacent free chunks in same slab and merge. low overhead and reduces medium-sized fragmentation.
kai: note: coalescer must be NUMA-aware on multi-gpu hosts and not block critical threads. can schedule on background GC thread with rate limits.
monica: rollout plan: 1) enable allocator probe + histograms (canary) 2) apply kv_prefill_soft_cap 10% traffic 3) run stress jobs and collect results 4) enable slab-coalescer on canary for 24h 5) promote if OK.
sahil: will post the experimental results in this thread. also adding a small dashboard: bin occupancy over time + p95 latency + OOM count.
alex: action items: @sahil run stress and add dashboard; @kai prototype soft-cap patch + fallback route PR; @monica add ci perf-guard and own rollouts; I'll prototype coalescer.
monica: thanks. if we see regressions on cost, we can tune batching heuristics (smaller batches for long seqs) to reduce peak working set.
ka i: small correction to action list: PRs should include a toggle flag `allocator_frag_debug` and telemetry to avoid alert fatigue.
alex: agreed. tagging this thread as the canonical conversation for this run. I'll upload the alloc histograms once sahil's job finishes. :thumbsup:
